cultural.vision_reason: The piece is a woven silk and silver-thread textile strip made in Safavid Iran (early 1600s), a Persian silk textile despite the misleading "Turkish" title reference; the object itself is a Persian-made silk furnishing textile, so it belongs to the claimed culture.

physical.title: Surround for Turkish Silk Cushion Cover
physical.medium_raw: Silk, silver-metal thread: plain weave with inner warps and with continuous and discontinuous supplementary wefts bound in plain and 1/3 Z twill order
physical.summary: Surround for Turkish Silk Cushion Cover, early 1600s. Iran, Safavid period (1501–1722). Silk, silver-metal thread: plain weave with inner warps and with continuous and discontinuous supplementary wefts bound in plain and 1/3 Z twill order; overall: 139.7 x 22.9 cm (55 x 9 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, Andrew R. and Martha Holden Jennings Fund, 2007.13.2
